title: Hassler Roma vs Hotel de la Ville: Neighbors on the Steps (2026) | Suites With Keith
description: Hotel Hassler Roma vs Hotel de la Ville, next-door neighbors at the top of the Spanish Steps, compared by a travel advisor who visited both in October 2026: rooftops, style, rooms, spa, and who each one suits.

hero.alt: The Spanish Steps and Trinità dei Monti at sunrise, with Hotel Hassler Roma at the top of the Steps
Hotel de la Ville’s courtyard, with red and white striped umbrellas and salmon-pink walls with green shutters

sub: Next-door neighbors at the top of the Spanish Steps, with the same crowds outside. The difference is style, the rooftop, and whether you want a spa this year. Here is how I would choose.

choose.h3: If you want traditional grandeur and a Michelin star
choose.lead: A very nice, very traditional luxury hotel right at the top of the Steps, with a Michelin-starred restaurant on the roof and a beautiful one in the courtyard.
choose.alt: A Hotel Hassler Roma bedroom with a fabric-covered canopy bed, damask walls and a gilded frame

choose.h3: If you want color, a rooftop bar and a spa
choose.lead: A Rocco Forte in an 18th-century palazzo with colorful, very Roman interiors, Cielo on the roof for sunset drinks, and a Sicilian-inspired spa.
choose.alt: A Hotel de la Ville salon with yellow walls hung with engravings and a black and white marble floor

pitch: Work with me and you get Fora perks, plus someone who knows these hotels personally and personalizes your stay: I request the right room at either one, tell you when the Hassler’s new wellness area opens, and arrange your transfers from Fiumicino or Termini. Same rate as booking direct.

band.h2: Same Steps, same crowds. Do you want tradition or color?
paras: The Hassler is very traditional, and that’s the appeal. The dining is the highlight, with a Michelin-starred restaurant on the roof.
Hotel de la Ville is next door, with colorful, very Roman interiors and Cielo, a rooftop bar and restaurant with views all over the city. It also has a spa now, while the Hassler’s opens in 2027.

If you love grand-hotel style and a serious dinner, pick the Hassler. If you want a more colorful palazzo, a rooftop bar for sunset and a spa this trip, pick the de la Ville. And if you are deciding between the Rocco Forte hotels, I prefer the de la Ville’s sister, the de Russie.

guide.alt: A freestanding tub in a black marble Hotel Hassler Roma bathroom, with windows over the rooftops to St. Peter’s
paras: The Hassler has a Michelin-starred restaurant on the roof, with the rooftops of Rome laid out below you.
At Hotel de la Ville, the highlight is Cielo, the rooftop bar and restaurant across the top two floors, with views across Rome’s skyline. Come for sunset drinks.

guide.alt: Hotel de la Ville’s reception, with a marble desk, plaster reliefs on sage walls and a black and white zigzag floor
paras: Hotel de la Ville is an 18th-century palazzo with interiors by Tommaso Ziffer: yellow walls, engravings, plaster reliefs and black and white floors. There are 104 rooms and suites, some with terraces and city views.
The Hassler is classic luxury for travelers who want Rome’s grand-hotel style: canopy beds, damask walls and crystal lamps, and bathrooms that open to the trees.

guide.alt: A Hotel de la Ville bathroom with a freestanding tub, marble walls and a double vanity
paras: Hotel de la Ville has a Sicilian-inspired spa.
The Hassler is building a large new wellness and gym area that opens in 2027. Until then, if a spa and gym matter a lot, I point people to the Bulgari or the Corinthia.

guide.alt: A bright Hotel Hassler Roma bathroom with a double vanity and a balcony door open to the trees
paras: At both, you step out the door into the crowds at the top of the Steps, from morning to night. That is the trade for an address you can’t beat for being central.
If quiet matters more than the Steps, the Eden is a few minutes away on a calm residential street. At the Hassler, the courtyard restaurant is a calmer place to eat than the streets outside.

faq.q: Which is better, the Hassler or Hotel de la Ville?
faq.a: It depends on your style. The Hassler for very traditional luxury and Michelin-starred dining on the roof. Hotel de la Ville for colorful Roman interiors, the Cielo rooftop bar and a spa you can use now.

faq.q: Are they really next to each other?
faq.a: Yes. Both are at the top of the Spanish Steps, and the Hassler is right next door to Hotel de la Ville.
For dinner, the Hassler’s Michelin-starred restaurant. For sunset drinks, Cielo at Hotel de la Ville, across the top two floors with views all over the city.
Hotel de la Ville, with a Sicilian-inspired spa. The Hassler’s new wellness and gym area opens in 2027.

faq.q: Is there a better Rocco Forte option?
faq.a: For me, yes: Hotel de Russie, the de la Ville’s sister a few minutes away. Its large courtyard, renovated rooms and spa with an indoor pool made it the stronger stay.
